/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 24 April 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2665 (-8)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4282 (-33)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1960 (-5)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1535 (13)
Baltic Handysize Index: 797 (6)
CAPESIZE
The market eased into the weekend on a quieter note, with limited activity across both basins and a slightly softer undertone developing in the Atlantic. The BCI 182 5TC slipped by $301 to close at $38,836, reflecting a lack of fresh momentum rather than any sharp deterioration in fundamentals. In the Pacific, conditions remained steady but subdued. The C5 route was effectively flat, edging up by just $0.005 to $13.000. Activity was thin, with only one major miner present and showing little urgency, while an operator was heard bidding around $13.00 against offers at $13.40, indicative of a balanced market rather than any meaningful tension. The Atlantic basin was similarly quiet but characterised more by a degree of standoff between charterers and owners. The C3 index eased by $0.150 to $33.068, with a clearer gap in pricing emerging, as bids hovered around $32.50 against offers closer to $34.00. Despite the softer tone, ballaster supply for May loaders remains tight, continuing to lend underlying support.
PANAMAX
As the week came to a close, there was a split in sentiment between the Atlantic and Pacific. In the Atlantic, the North Continent tonnage build up is still evident, brokers said. Mineral and grain trades in the Atlantic for prompt dates appear to have largely cleared out, which is now pushing bids for any remaining business lower. Fronthaul is reflecting a similar trend, with a growing list of available tonnage. Market participants report softening bids, and owners are increasingly revising their offers downward in an effort to secure cover. In Asia, the market remained firm as consistent tonnage demand and earlier fixtures continue to support market sentiment. Indonesian exports are still active and would appear to be more than sufficient to meet the growing supply of available tonnage. Couple this with an also active Australian and North Pacific markets and the result is an upward moving bid. The P3A increased today by $86 and the P5 also went up by $220. Period activity has been evident with Bunge reported to have taken the Adriatica Graeca II (82,000 2026) Dalian 30 April for 8/10 months redeliver worldwide at around $21,000. The Capt Stefanos (74,077 2002) Nansha 15 May was said to have fixed in direct continuation for 4/6 months although further information failed to surface. The P5TC fell by $44 to conclude the week at $17,638.

Asia
GCL Icon (82,567 2021) Zhoushan 24/25 April is reported to have fixed an Australian round voyage with coal in $20,000’s. Similarly, the Shun Chang (93,322 2010) Yantai also fixed via Australia to Southeast Asia in the mid-low $17,000’s to Cobelfret. The Xiangming (74,133 2001) CJK 6 May was heard to have covered a stem via the Russian Far East at $20,000 but further information was lacking. Finally, the scrubber fitted Raraka (76,064 2012) open in Shanghai 21/22 April fixed a coal stem from East Coast Australia to South China at $15,500 but the charterer and scrubber benefit remains unclear.
SUPRAMAX
The end of a firm week across the Atlantic and Pacific basins saw sentiment remain generally positive. Some brokers spoke of an adjustment in expectations with the changed bunker costs, also with the various functions coming up in Geneva early next week many had left their desks early. The Asian arena finished the week on a high with positive demand remaining in play. The SSI Interceptor (63,896 2023) was heard fixed for a trip via Indonesia redelivery WC India - Pakistan at $27,500. The Mandarin River (56,774 2011) open Ningbo 1/5 May was heard to have been placed on subjects for a backhaul redelivery West Africa in the low $17,000s. The XI HU (63,519 2019) open Qinzhou 24 April was heard to have failed for a trip to Bangladesh at $30,000 with clinker. The JC Peace (53,299 2005) open Caofeidian 29 April / 5 May was also placed on subjects redelivery Red Sea at around $20,000, but no more details surfaced. Elsewhere, the Tomini Liberty (63,511 2018) open Kandla 28 April was also heard to be on subjects for South Africa to Far East at $17,000. From last week, the SSI Interceptor (63,896 2023) was heard fixed for trip via Indonesia redelivery WC India - Pakistan at $27,500, but no more details surfaced. Period activity remained in play, the Lowlands Freedom (64,481 2023) open Kashima 26/29 April was fixed for 19-21 months trading at $17,250 with Dreyfus. Also, the African Kite (61,413 2013) open Villanueva 29/30 April was rumoured on subjects for 4/6 months with redelivery Singapore/Japan at $21,500. The 11TC average finished the week up $162 at $19,403.
HANDYSIZE
The week ended on a firm note, despite limited fresh activity across both the Atlantic and Asian regions. The BHSI increased by 6 points to 797, while the 7TC average rose by $119 to close at $14,354. Conditions in the Continent and Mediterranean remained broadly stable, with rates holding in line with earlier levels. Although fixture volumes were relatively light, the U.S. Gulf and South Atlantic continued to demonstrate underlying strength across all vessel sizes, with both owners and charterers gradually firming their rate expectations. In Asia, activity was similarly subdued, with few fresh developments reported. Nevertheless, charterers were still seen bidding slightly above previous fixtures, supporting an overall firm market tone. On the fixtures side, the Locomotion (38,046 2013), open Inchon 23 April, was fixed for a voyage to Southeast Asia at $16,000. Meanwhile, the TSL Lusaha (35,947 2015), open Hong Kong 27 April, secured a trip into Australia at $16,000, with no further details disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
World Crude Steel Production

Global crude steel output stood 4.2% below the same month last year at 159.9 Mt in March, bringing 1q26 production 2.3% lower year-on-year to 458.9 Mt, World Steel Association data show. During the first three months of the year, Chinese and Japanese output dipped 4.6% and 1.7% on the year to 247.4 Mt and 20.1 Mt, respectively. In contrast, Indian production rose 10.8% to 44.7 Mt, while North American output lifted 2.4% to 23.6 Mt in 1q26.

Trading Commentary
Cape
A frantic day for Cape paper with heavy downside flow throughout the day. May opened at $33250, and offered heavily down to its intra-day low of $31000 (-$2,250) before closing at $31500 (-$1,750), trading over 2300 lots. Jun traded $32750 down to $31250 (-$1,500), with lows of $31000 (-$1,750). Q3 was active, closing at $29100 (-$1,450) with lows of $28350 (-$2,200). Q34 saw the most activity with over 3000 lots traded, closing at $29150 (-$1,350), with lows of $28250 (-$2,200). Cal27 traded $25500-$25000 closing at $25300 (-$350).

PMX
The Pmx curve moved lower across the board today, with bids pulling back on uncertainty before finding some support into the close. May traded down to 18500 from an early high of 19200, finishing around 18700, while Jun ranged from 19400 down to 18800, then recovering slightly to close 19100. Q3 traded from 18700 to 18300, while Q4 held a relatively tighter range between 17250 and 16800. On the back end, Cal 27 printed between 14500 and 14750. Overall, the market saw broad pressure early on, before stabilising to close the week out.

SMX + HANDY
A subdued end to the week the physical market quietened down encouraging sellers to aggress the available premium. Aided but the sell off on the larger sizes, the nearby smx came under pressure with May trading 18100 on open and June 18000, down to lows of 17850 and 17650. Q3 treaded to a low of 16450 with Q34 sold at 15900. The market lacked any conviction during the afternoon session with the majority of the days volume all done pre index. Cal 27 slipped below 13k trading at 12950. Handy Q34 was one of the few contracts to hold its value trading up to 14500 a number of times as the S/H spread narrows.

Market Fundamentals
World Crude Steel Production
Global crude steel output stood 4.2% below the same month
last year at 159.9 Mt in March, bringing 1q26 production
2.3% lower year-on-year to 458.9 Mt, World Steel Association
data show. During the ﬁrst three months of the year, Chinese
and Japanese output dipped 4.6% and 1.7% on the year to
247.4 Mt and 20.1 Mt, respectively. In contrast, Indian
production rose 10.8% to 44.7 Mt, while North American
output lifted 2.4% to 23.6 Mt in 1q26.
Trading Commentary
Cape
A frantic day for Cape paper with heavy downside ﬂow
throughout the day. May opened at $33250, and oﬀered
heavily down to its intra-day low of $31000 (-$2,250) before
closing at $31500 (-$1,750), trading over 2300 lots. Jun traded
$32750 down to $31250 (-$1,500), with lows of $31000
(-$1,750). Q3 was active, closing at $29100 (-$1,450) with lows
of $28350 (-$2,200). Q34 saw the most activity with over 3000
lots traded, closing at $29150 (-$1,350), with lows of $28250
(-$2,200). Cal27 traded $25500-$25000 closing at $25300
(-$350).
PMX
The Pmx curve moved lower across the board today, with
bids pulling back on uncertainty before ﬁnding some
support into the close. May traded down to 18500 from an
early high of 19200, ﬁnishing around 18700, while Jun
ranged from 19400 down to 18800, then recovering slightly
to close 19100. Q3 traded from 18700 to 18300, while Q4
held a relatively tighter range between 17250 and 16800. On
the back end, Cal 27 printed between 14500 and 14750.
Overall, the market saw broad pressure early on, before
stabilising to close the week out.
SMX + HANDY
A subdued end to the week the physical market quietened
down encouraging sellers to aggress the available premium.
Aided but the sell oﬀ on the larger sizes, the nearby smx
came under pressure with May trading 18100 on open and
June 18000, down to lows of 17850 and 17650. Q3 treaded to
a low of 16450 with Q34 sold at 15900. The market lacked
any conviction during the afternoon session with the
majority of the days volume all done pre index. Cal 27
slipped below 13k trading at 12950. Handy Q34 was one of
the few contracts to hold its value trading up to 14500 a
number of times as the S/H spread narrows.Cape 180 5TC

Capesize Report24th April 2026
PAC: Quiet         ATL: Softer
Market Comments
After a busy week in the Paciﬁc, Friday opened to a very quiet market with
only the Dampier Major to be seen, though remained unﬁxed for the day.
Some operators looked to secure their mid May C5 stems sub $13s,
however after activity proved to be stagnant. A major ﬁxed their stem out
of Dongjiakou to Vietnam stem for 05/08 May at $6. Additionally, a tender
from Newcastle to China ﬁxed for 21/30 May in the high $18s region. One
major ﬁxed their 06/08 May stem from Zhanjiang to Vietnam, though the
rate remains elusive. A busy day for Nukes yesterday as conﬁrmation
came through that one charterer ﬁxing out of South Africa to China
secured a Newcastlemax on their C17 stem for 8/17 May at $24.75. Into
this morning June continues to sit at a discount to May, as Winning bids
laddered across the month from $32 to $31. An end user’s tender from
West Africa to China for tighter May dates heads to auction for a
consecutive day today.  a miner’s prompt Kamsar stem to China, however
details remain elusive moving into next week. It was conﬁrmed that an
end user’s transatlantic tender from Brazil to Egypt was ﬁxed, though
rates are unclear at this time. A 120/10 stem from Baltimore for 15/24 May

Capesize Report24th April 2026
Market Comments
A racing start in the Paciﬁc this week, as both volumes and freight peaked on Monday before gradually tailing oﬀ as the week
progressed. Two majors set the tone, amidst the backdrop of healthy cargo book and moderate tonnage. The former not
only built of C5 demand, but both solid peripheral iron ore and coal business. Early May dates the initial focus, as two present
majors each took a handful of vessels at $13.55-60 range. Operators contributed to volumes, with rates peaking at $13.75 on
larger tonnage. Mid $13’s were again ﬁxed on Tuesday, albeit marginally lower at $13.40-45. The same two majors again
taking a handful each. Volumes were steady day on day but the $0.15 loss started the trajectory of freight for the week, that
was never reversed. Newcastle business picked two stems ﬁxed to Taean and Putian at $21.71 and high $18’s, respectively.
Less willing to engage at mid $13.00’s C5, operators kicked oﬀ mid-week activity, initially ﬁnding vessels at $13.20-30 range
before the majors only singles each at $13.10 range. East Australian ﬁxtures almost outweighed C5, however rates remained
elusive. Despite no major change to fundamentals in the East, pressure remained on the oﬀer as the majors aimed to break
$13. Initial optimism, stemming from an operator’s low $13 C5 ﬁxture on Thursday was short lived after the Dampier major
managed to ﬁnd an owner eager to break $13 and ﬁxing them at $12.90. Peripheral routes similarly drifted as the usual
major from TRMT, ﬁxed their Teluk to China stem at low $10.00’s, despite paying low $11.00’s on Monday. Similarly, re-
positional rates drifted from $10.00 to high $9.00’s for Indonesia to India business. As the week concluded, a major out of
Zhanjiang ﬁxed their stem for 06/08 May dates to Dung Quat - however, rates remained elusive.
An impressive replenishment of cargo through Monday morning, ensuring the very ﬁrm tone in the South was maintained.
Tonnage conversely was incredibly thin, particularly for mid-May. Unable to replenish this window of tonnage, it was end May
and into June that saw an inﬂux of vessels as owner’s raced to free tonnage to capitalise on the attractive South Atlantic rates.
Owner’s optimism was reﬂected in the collection of $34.75 C3 oﬀers on standard capes, whilst larger tonnage sat $1 below.
Hopes of repeating Friday’s heights were dashed early on Tuesday, as the usual major from Sudeste found a Newcastlemax
at high $32 C3 equivalent for mid May. For similar dates, a trader ﬁxed a standard cape at $32.90 C3, after being hit almost
immediately $0.15 above their bid. Albeit a Brazil only cargo, the attitude reﬂected owner’s eagerness to lock in the $32-33 C3
range, in a market of very few bids. The latter point understandable, as operators and traders alike were not eager to chase
oﬀers as physical traded at $350k to paper. More Brazil only cargoes were ﬁxed mid-week, many of which not your traditional
stems. Including Ubu to Taiwan and to Kwangyang. In additional, a miner took a trader’s vessel at $32.95 C3 equivalent for
an Acu to Qingdao stem end May, whilst the usual miner from Itaguai found a Newcastlemax at $33. Mid to end May oﬀers
drifted closer to $34 come Thursday on standards, as the week’s sporadic ﬁxtures chipped away at the C3. June saw an
equivalent discount. Despite the softer tone, an end user’s Newcastlemax manage to lock in a solid $32.90 C3 rate for a
Freetown stem, whilst a tender from Sudeste ﬁxed at mid $32.00’s. The ﬁrmest of the lot, a Newcastlemax ﬁxed for C17
business $0.60 higher than index, at $24.60.
Fronhauls bolstered the North Atlantic cargo book on Monday, supported by a handful of transatlantic and backhaul stems.
April tonnage remained undeniably tight, not really moderating until 05 May onwards. Tight from the outset, the North
showed no sign nor did it soften throughout the week. With fundamentals clear, the usual end-user from Port Cartier
engaged a trader’s vessel early on ﬁxing her for fronthaul. Opinion on rates varied from $42 to $44, however even the lower
end clear $63,000 C9 equivalent. Tranastlantic business took the fore on Tuesday, as a German end-user took a vessel for
their short early May, Narvik to Rotterdam stem at $8.40. This ran to $51,300 as a round but when adjusted to 30 days, was
closer to $44,800 or $250k proﬁt over the curve. This drove a sizable increase in the C8 index. Demand remained healthy mid-
week, however Panamax continued to aggressively price and resultantly saw a Sept-Iles to Djen-Djen cargo split. This trend
continued into the latter half of the week, placing charterers able to employ this option in a very advantageous position.
Despite a robust cargo book, volumes slumped into the latter half of the week. Amidst the silence on Friday, the curve
endured an early morning sell oﬀ which further discouraged any physical bidding to close oﬀ the week.

Handysize/Supramax Report24th April 2026
63,500 Atlantic: FIRMER      Paciﬁc: FIRMER           38,000 Atlantic: FIRMER      Paciﬁc: FLAT
Atlantic Comment
The Baltic Dry Index (BDI) surged to a four-month high this week, reaching 2,633 points as the
market enjoyed its 12th consecutive session of gains. This rally was fuelled by a massive 11% spike
in the Capesize segment, where daily earnings soared past $35,000 due to a pre-May rush for iron
ore and coal. While a fragile ceaseﬁre in the Middle East has allowed a limited number of ships to
begin navigating the Strait of Hormuz, the broader freight market remains under pressure from
bunker volatility. Global marine fuel prices continue to hover near record highs, meaning that while
freight rates look impressive, a signiﬁcant portion of those gains is being swallowed by refuelling
costs. Meanwhile, Brazil’s record 178-milliontonne harvest is providing the necessary volume to
keep the Atlantic market tight, as a wall of grain continues to move toward Asia.
On the Continent Handysize market, rates have remained ﬁrm, with scrap ﬁxtures providing the
main support. However, ballasters from the Mediterranean have limited further gains. We saw a
37,000 deadweight vessel ﬁx basis Skaw for a scrap run to the Mediterranean at USD 17,000, which
is around USD 500 higher compared to levels seen last week. On the Supramax and Ultramax
market, the week started on a softer footing due to increased vessel availability. However, as the
week progressed, activity picked up with a fresh ﬂow of cargo. We are seeing scrap runs to the
Mediterranean being discussed at levels above USD 20,000, although we did see a 63,000
deadweight vessel ﬁx basis Amsterdam to redeliver in the Mediterranean with scrap at USD 19,500.
In the Mediterranean Handysize market, rates have remained ﬁrm this week, although sentiment
remains mixed. Owners continue to hold strong ideas, supported by ﬁrmer conditions in the
Atlantic basin, while a thinning cargo book and increased vessel availability in the Mediterranean
are making it harder to maintain these levels consistently. We are still seeing tonnage ballast from
the East to the West Mediterranean in search of scrap business, although demand here appears to
be easing, with many stems being covered in house. We saw a 37,000 deadweight vessel rate a trip
from the East Mediterranean to the Spore/Japan range at USD 16,000, versus charterer ideas of
USD 13,500, with charterer ideas USD 500 higher compared to ﬁxing levels on similar routes last
week. On the larger sizes, tonnage availability remains high and out of balance, putting pressure
on rates. We are seeing charterers rate Ultramaxes for a trip from the East Mediterranean to India
at USD 17,000, around USD 500 lower than levels seen on similar routes last week.
The East Coast South America (ECSA) Handysize market has maintained its upward trajectory this
week, bolstered by an extensive cargo list that has kept owners ﬁrmly in control. Reﬂecting this
heat, coastal runs for Recalada towards North Brazil have now broken the $20,000/day barrier as
charterers scramble for coverage. The strength of the region was further underscored by a
standout ﬁxture where a large eco Handysize achieved over $25,000/day with delivery Recalada for
a trip toward the West Coast of South America (WCSA). The Supramax and Ultramax segments in
the East Coast South America market experienced a notable shift in momentum this week. The
period opened with a heavy tone as a surge of new tonnage entering the region initially dampened
sentiment, however by Wednesday, the market pivoted into a scramble for beginning-May ETAs.
This sudden tightening has signiﬁcantly pushed rates, with modern Eco Ultramaxes now
commanding levels in the high $27,000s for trips loading in North Brazil toward the East
Mediterranean. Across the Atlantic, West Africa has also seen a resurgence in activity. Mining
operations, which had previously slowed their output amid the extreme volatility of bunker prices,
have returned to the market with fresh inquiries.
It has been a cautiously active week in the USG Handy market, the tonnage count is slightly down
from last week, and while market circulated orders have also been lower than last week, there have
been some orders that charterers have kept oﬀ market. A few charterers have found themselves
needing spot/ppt replacements, and others have requirements for early May loading dates that
they are keeping behind the curtains. Overall sentiment remains quietly positive, with owners
continuing to push ﬁrmer ideas amid a relatively balanced position list. Fuel uncertainty continues
to weigh on sentiment across the region as the market keeps a close eye on developments in the
Middle East. We are seeing Trans-Atlantic trips rate for USD 13,000 – in line with levels at the start
of the week. On the Supramax and Ultramax market, conditions have remained ﬁrm. While fresh 1–
10 May positions have entered the market, increased inter-Caribbean enquiry has helped support
rates, pushing levels into the mid USD 20,000s. We are also seeing Trans-Atlantic trips ﬁxing at
around USD 30,000 on an Ultramax. Fronthaul activity, however, remains limited.

Handysize/Supramax Report24th April 2026
Paciﬁc Comments
This week, the Paciﬁc Supramax market experienced a strong upward surge, with the overall market sentiment turning decisively bullish and freight rates across all major routes recording
substantial gains. A pronounced “tonnage shortage” sentiment emerged, particularly in Southeast Asia and the North Paciﬁc. Previously suppressed trading demand was released in a
concentrated manner, and when combined with temporary tightness in vessel supply, drove the market sharply higher within a short period, resulting in a clear upward shift in the earnings
benchmark.
The Indonesian coal sector was the ﬁrst to reﬂect this upward momentum. As fresh cargoes gradually entered the market while early-positioned tonnage in Southeast Asia remained limited, the
resulting supply-demand mismatch pushed rates higher. The Indo/SE Asia route strengthened continuously from the beginning of the week, with reported ﬁxtures such as an SMX open Weda
ﬁxing in the high USD 18k range for Indo/Thai, and another SMX open Obi Island ﬁxing up to USD 20k, highlighting strong regional demand and rapid tonnage absorption. On the Indo/China
route, although domestic supply-demand fundamentals remained relatively balanced and import demand was not particularly strong, freight levels still increased notably in line with the
broader market. The Indo/India route showed the most signiﬁcant gains, with rates leading the rally and even surpassing the USD 30k mark. Reported ﬁxtures include a UMX open Philippines
ﬁxing at USD 31k for Indo/Bdesh, as well as an SMX delivery Singapore on subs above USD 30k for Indo/WCI, clearly reﬂecting robust demand from the Indian subcontinent and a tight tonnage
situation.
The North Vietnam/South China region continued to act as a core supporting pillar for the market, maintaining high levels of activity. Clinker exports from Vietnam to Bangladesh remained
strong, with rates moving further upward, including a reported UMX open Zhoushan ﬁxing around USD 26k for clinker via South China to Bdesh. At the same time, nickel ore shipments
sustained strong momentum, with SMX open South China ﬁxing at USD 19k+ for nickel ore to China, continuing to absorb regional tonnage. In addition, backhaul demand to the United States
also strengthened, with a UMX open Yangjiang ﬁxing at USD 21k for steels to USEC, indicating solid support from long-haul demand.
The NOPAC market remained stable overall. Although trading activity was relatively limited, freight levels moved upward in line with the broader market trend. UMX open Far East ﬁxtures were
reported at USD 19k+ for NOPAC round voyages, providing a solid ﬂoor for the market.
North China steel and general cargo exports strengthened signiﬁcantly this week, particularly on routes to the Red Sea and the Mediterranean. Fixtures included an SMX open North China
ﬁxing around USD 22k to the Mediterranean via Goa with bagged cargo, and another SMX open Zhoushan ﬁxing around USD 19k to the Mediterranean via Goa with steels, demonstrating
strong long-haul demand pulling tonnage away from the region. Bulk cargoes also remained ﬁrm, with a UMX open North China ﬁxing around USD 27k for a trip to Bangladesh with slag,
indicating a market that was not only strong but arguably approaching overheated levels.
The Australian market also maintained a ﬁrm tone this week, with stable cargo ﬂows from the supply side. Grain and salt from Western Australia, coal from Eastern Australia, and minerals from
Northern Australia continued to move steadily, providing consistent support to the regional market and lifting overall freight levels. A reported ﬁxture includes a UMX open Philippines ﬁxing
around USD 23.5k for WAus/China salt, reﬂecting the broader strength across routes.
In the period market, strength persisted throughout the week. Supported by the rising spot market and ﬁrm FFA levels, period rates continued to climb. UMX short period ﬁxtures were
commonly concluded at USD 20k–21k, while one-year period rates increased to USD 18.5k+, reﬂecting strong owner conﬁdence in the near- to mid-term outlook and a clear reluctance to
commit tonnage.
Overall, the Paciﬁc Supramax market this week was characterized by rapid gains and broad-based strength, driven by concentrated demand release and temporary tightness in vessel supply. In
the short term, with cargo volumes continuing to emerge and market sentiment remaining strong, the market is expected to stay elevated, with potential for further upside. However, caution is
warranted regarding the risk of a short-term correction following the sharp rally, as well as the impact of macroeconomic developments on market dynamics.

After the recent strength seen in domestic steel markets, it is disappointing to
witness a softening over the past few days, with declines of USD 8 –10 per ton
being recorded in both India and Bangladesh, and even more pronounced reduc-
tions in Pakistan.

On the sale front, there has been an en -bloc transaction involving three Woodchip
Carriers, concluded on an as is basis in Hon Gai, Vietnam. The vessels involved
are the “Godspeed 6666” (10,348 lwt), the “Hao Hung 66” (7,807 lwt) and the
“Hao Hung 01” (4,997 lwt), all reportedly committed at a level of USD 439 per lwt.

The Fednav -controlled “Federal Yamaska” (10,688 lwt) has also been sold, on
private terms, in a damaged condition for recycling in Canada, with delivery ex-
pected to take place under tow.

Enquiry continues across the three Sub -Continent markets; however, the ongoing
uncertainty surrounding the on/off ceasefire in the Middle East has resulted in a
cautious, wait -and-see approach being adopted by many recyclers. At the same
time, there has been a noticeable slowdown in tonnage being placed to the mar-
ket, with the majority of available units falling within the medium -size segment.

In Turkey, most recycling yards are currently operating at or near full capacity, with
a number of vessels already waiting at anchorage for berths. As a result, enquiry
levels have effectively turned negative, with little appetite for additional tonnage in
the short term.

From a broader perspective, this remains a challenging environment for buyers.
There is a growing view that the current market may be masking underlying pres-
sures, with the full economic impact of recent Middle East developments yet to be
realised. Should stability return in the near term, it is possible that a number of
deferred recycling candidates could begin to enter the market. In such a scenario,
scrapping volumes may gradually increase, with the potential for a more active
period emerging into 2027.

World Crude Steel Production
Global crude steel output stood 4.2% below the same month last year at 159.9 Mt in March, bringing 1q26 production 2.3% lower
year-on-year to 458.9 Mt, World Steel Association data show. During the first three months of the year, Chinese and Japanese out put
dipped 4.6% and 1.7% on the year to 247.4 Mt and 20.1 Mt, respectively. In contrast, Indian production rose 10.8% to 44.7 Mt,
while North American output lifted 2.4% to 23.6 Mt in 1q26.

ARA clean oil product stocks fall to lowest level since February 2024
At the Amsterdam -Rotterdam -Antwerp (ARA) storage hub, clean oil product inventories declined by 80KT w -o-w to 3.94MT during the
week ending 23 April, the lowest level since February 2024, according to data from Refinitiv. Gasoil and naphtha stocks decre ased
by 90KT w -o-w to 1.86MT and by 50KT w -o-w to 380KT respectively. Jet fuel inventories were also down by 20KT w -o-w to 580KT,
whereas gasoline stocks grew by 70KT w -o-w to 1.11MT.

items.parsed_text: Panam ax/Kamsarmax Report24th April 2026 ATL: SOFT PAC: FLAT/FIRMER MID EAST: FLATMarket Comments ATL SHORT LOOKING AHEAD, THE COMING WEEK IS EXPECTED TO BE SOMEWHAT DISRUPTED DUE TO HOLIDAYS AND MANY TRAVELLING FOR GENEVA DRY. THIS IS FURTHER COMPOUNDED BY THE NEGATIVE SENTIMENT FILTERING IN FROM THE CAPE SECTOR, PARTICULARLY FOLLOWING REPORTS OF THE GUINEAN GOVERNMENT LIMITING EXPORTS. AS A RESULT, WE EXPECT THE MARKET TO FACE ADDITIONAL DOWNWARD PRESSURE UNLESS THERE IS A CLEAR AND SUSTAINED INCREASE IN DEMAND TO COUNTERBALANCE THE CURRENT TONE. PACIFIC SHORT REPORT: THE SOUTH HAS BEEN ACTIVE AND FIRM THIS WEEK, DRIVEN BY TIGHT VESSEL SUPPLY AND STRONG INDO/SCHINA-SEASIA CARGO DEMAND. ALTHOUGH INDO/INDIA FLOW HAS SLOWED, INCREASED SCHINA/INDIA LIMESTONE SHIPMENTS HAVE PROVIDED SOME SUPPORT. IN CONTRAST, IT HAS BEEN LESS DYNAMIC IN THE NORTH, THOUGH NOPAC EXPERIENCED INITIAL GAINS EARLY IN THE WEEK, LEVELS FLATTENED OUT SOON AFTERWARDS. ECAUS COAL SAW SOFTER ACTIVITY AND LIMITED CARGOES IN THE NEAR TERM, THOUGH DEMAND APPEARS TO IMPROVE FOR MID-MAY ONWARD. DEMAND REMAINED STEADY THROUGHOUT THE WEEK, PROVIDING A CONSISTENT LEVEL OF ACTIVITY, BUT IT WAS NOT STRONG ENOUGH TO GENERATE ANY MEANINGFUL UPWARD MOMENTUM ON RATES OR SHIFT SENTIMENT SIGNIFICANTLY. 2A - THE ROUTE REMAINED ACTIVE THIS WEEK, SUPPORTED BY CONTINUED BUYING INTEREST FROM FAR EAST OPERATORS. HOWEVER, THE VOLUME OF AVAILABLE TONNAGE PROVED TOO HEAVY TO SUSTAIN FURTHER GAINS, AND THE MARKET SOFTENED SLIGHTLY AS THE WEEK PROGRESSED. WHILE WE ENDED LAST WEEK SEEING HIGHS IN THE 26S, MORE RECENT REPORTS INDICATE UNITS FIXING IN THE 24S RANGE. P6 - IT WAS ANOTHER LACKLUSTRE WEEK FOR THE ROUTE, WITH DEMAND STAYING NOTABLY QUIET DESPITE A REASONABLY SHORT TONNAGE LIST. THE ABSENCE OF FIRM BIDDING INTEREST FORCED OWNERS TO GRADUALLY REDUCE THEIR OFFERS IN ORDER TO SECURE COVERAGE. BY FRIDAY MORNING, THE ROUTE HAD TRADED DOWN WELL INTO THE LOW 18S P6 EQUIVALENT, REFLECTING THE SOFTER OVERALL SENTIMENT. 1A/2A/P6 14123/25223/18473 Simpson Spence Young Ltd T: +44 (0)20 7977 7400 E: panamax@ssyglobal.comWhile reasonable care has been taken to ensure that the information in this publication is accurate, SSY can accept no responsibility for any errors or omissions or any consequences arising therefrom. Please click here to view our terms and conditions in section 6.2.Dry Cargo Report Panam ax/Kamsarmax Report24th April 2026 Pacific Comment PACIFIC LONG REPORT: THE SOUTH HAS BEEN BOOMING THIS WEEK WHEREAS THE PACE IN THE NORTH HAS BEEN SLOWER WITH LOWER BUT STILL FIRM LEVELS. TONNAGE IN THE SOUTH HAS BEEN TIGHT THROUGHOUT THE WEEK, BE IT FOR MODERN OR OVERAGED TONNAGE, WHILST INDO/SEASIA AND INDO/SCHINA HAS SEEN HEALTHY VOLUMES, LEADING TO STRONG APPETITE FOR SHIPS AND LEVELS PUSHING UP. EARLY IN THE WEEK, OA LME’S BEGAN ASKING 19-21K FROM INDIA AND SCHINA POSITIONS, AND SOON STARTED SEEING BIDS IN THE MID HIGH TEENS RANGE. LME’S OPENING IN SCHINA EASILY FIXED HIGH TEENS THROUGHOUT THE WEEK FOR A STANDARD INDO/SCHINA RUN WHILE SHIPS IN SEASIA WENT IN THE LOW 20’S. INDO/INDIA HAS GONE FAIRLY QUIET THIS WEEK, ALTHOUGH SCHINA/INDIA LIMESTONE STEMS HAVE INCREASED, PROVIDING SHIPS SEEKING REPOSITION TO THE WEST AN OUTLET. A MODERN KMX EX SCHINA WENT AT 21K FOR SUCH A RUN. AS WE WRAPPED UP THE WEEK, CHATTER ABOUT SPOT INDO/SCHINA TRADES HAS EMERGED, SEEMING TO POINT TOWARDS A ROSY START FOR THE COMING WEEK IN THE SOUTH. THAT, HOWEVER, COULD BE TEMPERED BY A LOWER VOLUME OF CARGOES TO INDIA AS THE MONSOON SEASON APPROACHES. IN THE NORTH, WE BEGAN THE WEEK WITH A LESS CLEAR DIRECTION. THE PACE WAS SLOWER WITHOUT THE EXCITEMENT THE SOUTH WAS EXPERIENCING. EVEN SO, WITH THE ONGOING SUPPORTIVE VOLUME OF NOPAC GRAINS AND A HANDFUL OF MINERAL STEMS, NOPAC LEVELS HAVE IMPROVED RIGHT AT THE START OF THE WEEK COMPARED TO WHERE IT ENDED LAST WEEK. EARLY ON, AN OA KMX EX NCHINA FIXED 17/17.5K FOR NOPAC/S-NCHINA (=18/18.5K P3) WHILE A 75/15 EX NCHINA FIXED A HEFTY 18K. AFTER THE INITIAL BOOST, LEVELS HAVE REMAINED RATHER FLAT THROUGHOUT THE WEEK, GOING AROUND LOW-MID TO MID 18K P3 MAINLY. ECAUSTRALIA, ON THE OTHER HAND, HAS BEEN LESS ACTIVE FOR THE 1H MAY WINDOW. WITH CARGOES BEING LIMITED, WHICH ALSO MEANT FEWER DRAFT RESTRICTED COAL CARGOES AROUND, WE HAVE SEEN SHALLOW POST-PANAMAXES EX FEAST GO AT RELATIVELY LIGHT LEVELS OF 20-21S THROUGHOUT THE WEEK. A PROMPT 85/23 EX JPN WENT AT 20K FOR AUS RV WHILST AN 85/22 EX JPN OPENING EARLY MAY WENT TRADING IN THE 21S VS 22S. 2H MAY ONWARDS, HOWEVER, LOOKS MORE ACTIVE. A BKI CJK TYPE OPENING AT THE END OF APR FOR MID-MAY LOADING DATES IS SEEING AROUND 19K ON THE BID FOR AN ECAUS RV AT THE END OF THE WEEK. During the first three months of the year, Chinese and Japanese output dipped 4.6% and 1.7% on the year to 247.4 Mt and 20.1 Mt, respectively. In contrast, Indian production rose 10.8% to 44.7 Mt, while North American output lifted 2.4% to 23.6 Mt in 1q26. Trading Commentary Cape A frantic day for Cape paper with heavy downside flow throughout the day. May opened at $33250, and offered heavily down to its intra-day low of $31000 (-$2,250) before closing at $31500 (-$1,750), trading over 2300 lots. Jun traded $32750 down to $31250 (-$1,500), with lows of $31000 (-$1,750). Q3 was active, closing at $29100 (-$1,450) with lows of $28350 (-$2,200). Q34 saw the most activity with over 3000 lots traded, closing at $29150 (-$1,350), with lows of $28250 (-$2,200). Cal27 traded $25500-$25000 closing at $25300 (-$350). PMX The Pmx curve moved lower across the board today, with bids pulling back on uncertainty before finding some support into the close. May traded down to 18500 from an early high of 19200, finishing around 18700, while Jun ranged from 19400 down to 18800, then recovering slightly to close 19100. Q3 traded from 18700 to 18300, while Q4 held a relatively tighter range between 17250 and 16800. On the back end, Cal 27 printed between 14500 and 14750. Overall, the market saw broad pressure early on, before stabilising to close the week out. SMX + HANDY A subdued end to the week the physical market quietened down encouraging sellers to aggress the available premium. Aided but the sell off on the larger sizes, the nearby smx came under pressure with May trading 18100 on open and June 18000, down to lows of 17850 and 17650. Q3 treaded to a low of 16450 with Q34 sold at 15900. The market lacked any conviction during the afternoon session with the majority of the days volume all done pre index. Cal 27 slipped below 13k trading at 12950. items.parsed_text: Capesize Report24th April 2026 PAC: Quiet ATL: Softer Market Comments After a busy week in the Pacific, Friday opened to a very quiet market with only the Dampier Major to be seen, though remained unfixed for the day. Some operators looked to secure their mid May C5 stems sub $13s, however after activity proved to be stagnant. A major fixed their stem out of Dongjiakou to Vietnam stem for 05/08 May at $6. Additionally, a tender from Newcastle to China fixed for 21/30 May in the high $18s region. One major fixed their 06/08 May stem from Zhanjiang to Vietnam, though the rate remains elusive. A busy day for Nukes yesterday as confirmation came through that one charterer fixing out of South Africa to China secured a Newcastlemax on their C17 stem for 8/17 May at $24.75. Into this morning June continues to sit at a discount to May, as Winning bids laddered across the month from $32 to $31. An end user’s tender from West Africa to China for tighter May dates heads to auction for a consecutive day today. a miner’s prompt Kamsar stem to China, however details remain elusive moving into next week. It was confirmed that an end user’s transatlantic tender from Brazil to Egypt was fixed, though rates are unclear at this time. A 120/10 stem from Baltimore for 15/24 May fixed yesterday afternoon in the low $41s region. The usual operator out of Bolivar secured their fronthaul stem to Korea for 12/21 May in the region of sub $40 and now look to find a vessel to fix a second cargo for the same dates. Friday saw demand in the North sparse heading into next week. Two majors set the tone, amidst the backdrop of healthy cargo book and moderate tonnage. The former not only built of C5 demand, but both solid peripheral iron ore and coal business. Early May dates the initial focus, as two present majors each took a handful of vessels at $13.55-60 range. Operators contributed to volumes, with rates peaking at $13.75 on larger tonnage. Mid $13’s were again fixed on Tuesday, albeit marginally lower at $13.40-45. The same two majors again taking a handful each. Volumes were steady day on day but the $0.15 loss started the trajectory of freight for the week, that was never reversed. Newcastle business picked two stems fixed to Taean and Putian at $21.71 and high $18’s, respectively. Less willing to engage at mid $13.00’s C5, operators kicked off mid-week activity, initially finding vessels at $13.20-30 range before the majors only singles each at $13.10 range. East Australian fixtures almost outweighed C5, however rates remained elusive. Despite no major change to fundamentals in the East, pressure remained on the offer as the majors aimed to break $13. Initial optimism, stemming from an operator’s low $13 C5 fixture on Thursday was short lived after the Dampier major managed to find an owner eager to break $13 and fixing them at $12.90. Peripheral routes similarly drifted as the usual major from TRMT, fixed their Teluk to China stem at low $10.00’s, despite paying low $11.00’s on Monday. Similarly, re- positional rates drifted from $10.00 to high $9.00’s for Indonesia to India business. As the week concluded, a major out of Zhanjiang fixed their stem for 06/08 May dates to Dung Quat - however, rates remained elusive. An impressive replenishment of cargo through Monday morning, ensuring the very firm tone in the South was maintained. Tonnage conversely was incredibly thin, particularly for mid-May. Unable to replenish this window of tonnage, it was end May and into June that saw an influx of vessels as owner’s raced to free tonnage to capitalise on the attractive South Atlantic rates. Owner’s optimism was reflected in the collection of $34.75 C3 offers on standard capes, whilst larger tonnage sat $1 below. Hopes of repeating Friday’s heights were dashed early on Tuesday, as the usual major from Sudeste found a Newcastlemax at high $32 C3 equivalent for mid May. For similar dates, a trader fixed a standard cape at $32.90 C3, after being hit almost immediately $0.15 above their bid. Albeit a Brazil only cargo, the attitude reflected owner’s eagerness to lock in the $32-33 C3 range, in a market of very few bids. The latter point understandable, as operators and traders alike were not eager to chase offers as physical traded at $350k to paper. More Brazil only cargoes were fixed mid-week, many of which not your traditional stems. Including Ubu to Taiwan and to Kwangyang. In additional, a miner took a trader’s vessel at $32.95 C3 equivalent for an Acu to Qingdao stem end May, whilst the usual miner from Itaguai found a Newcastlemax at $33. Mid to end May offers drifted closer to $34 come Thursday on standards, as the week’s sporadic fixtures chipped away at the C3. June saw an equivalent discount. Despite the softer tone, an end user’s Newcastlemax manage to lock in a solid $32.90 C3 rate for a Freetown stem, whilst a tender from Sudeste fixed at mid $32.00’s. The firmest of the lot, a Newcastlemax fixed for C17 business $0.60 higher than index, at $24.60. Fronhauls bolstered the North Atlantic cargo book on Monday, supported by a handful of transatlantic and backhaul stems. April tonnage remained undeniably tight, not really moderating until 05 May onwards. Tight from the outset, the North showed no sign nor did it soften throughout the week. With fundamentals clear, the usual end-user from Port Cartier engaged a trader’s vessel early on fixing her for fronthaul. Opinion on rates varied from $42 to $44, however even the lower end clear $63,000 C9 equivalent. Tranastlantic business took the fore on Tuesday, as a German end-user took a vessel for their short early May, Narvik to Rotterdam stem at $8.40. This ran to $51,300 as a round but when adjusted to 30 days, was closer to $44,800 or $250k profit over the curve. This drove a sizable increase in the C8 index. Demand remained healthy mid- week, however Panamax continued to aggressively price and resultantly saw a Sept-Iles to Djen-Djen cargo split. This trend continued into the latter half of the week, placing charterers able to employ this option in a very advantageous position. Despite a robust cargo book, volumes slumped into the latter half of the week. Amidst the silence on Friday, the curve endured an early morning sell off which further discouraged any physical bidding to close off the week. items.parsed_text: Handysize/Supramax Report24th April 2026 63,500 Atlantic: FIRMER Pacific: FIRMER 38,000 Atlantic: FIRMER Pacific: FLAT Atlantic Comment The Baltic Dry Index (BDI) surged to a four-month high this week, reaching 2,633 points as the market enjoyed its 12th consecutive session of gains. This rally was fuelled by a massive 11% spike in the Capesize segment, where daily earnings soared past $35,000 due to a pre-May rush for iron ore and coal. While a fragile ceasefire in the Middle East has allowed a limited number of ships to begin navigating the Strait of Hormuz, the broader freight market remains under pressure from bunker volatility. Global marine fuel prices continue to hover near record highs, meaning that while freight rates look impressive, a significant portion of those gains is being swallowed by refuelling costs. Meanwhile, Brazil’s record 178-milliontonne harvest is providing the necessary volume to keep the Atlantic market tight, as a wall of grain continues to move toward Asia. On the Continent Handysize market, rates have remained firm, with scrap fixtures providing the main support. However, ballasters from the Mediterranean have limited further gains. We saw a 37,000 deadweight vessel fix basis Skaw for a scrap run to the Mediterranean at USD 17,000, which is around USD 500 higher compared to levels seen last week. On the Supramax and Ultramax market, the week started on a softer footing due to increased vessel availability. However, as the week progressed, activity picked up with a fresh flow of cargo. We are seeing scrap runs to the Mediterranean being discussed at levels above USD 20,000, although we did see a 63,000 deadweight vessel fix basis Amsterdam to redeliver in the Mediterranean with scrap at USD 19,500. In the Mediterranean Handysize market, rates have remained firm this week, although sentiment remains mixed. Owners continue to hold strong ideas, supported by firmer conditions in the Atlantic basin, while a thinning cargo book and increased vessel availability in the Mediterranean are making it harder to maintain these levels consistently. We are still seeing tonnage ballast from the East to the West Mediterranean in search of scrap business, although demand here appears to be easing, with many stems being covered in house. We saw a 37,000 deadweight vessel rate a trip from the East Mediterranean to the Spore/Japan range at USD 16,000, versus charterer ideas of USD 13,500, with charterer ideas USD 500 higher compared to fixing levels on similar routes last week. On the larger sizes, tonnage availability remains high and out of balance, putting pressure on rates. We are seeing charterers rate Ultramaxes for a trip from the East Mediterranean to India at USD 17,000, around USD 500 lower than levels seen on similar routes last week. The East Coast South America (ECSA) Handysize market has maintained its upward trajectory this week, bolstered by an extensive cargo list that has kept owners firmly in control. Reflecting this heat, coastal runs for Recalada towards North Brazil have now broken the $20,000/day barrier as charterers scramble for coverage. The strength of the region was further underscored by a standout fixture where a large eco Handysize achieved over $25,000/day with delivery Recalada for a trip toward the West Coast of South America (WCSA). The Supramax and Ultramax segments in the East Coast South America market experienced a notable shift in momentum this week. The period opened with a heavy tone as a surge of new tonnage entering the region initially dampened sentiment, however by Wednesday, the market pivoted into a scramble for beginning-May ETAs. This sudden tightening has significantly pushed rates, with modern Eco Ultramaxes now commanding levels in the high $27,000s for trips loading in North Brazil toward the East Mediterranean. Across the Atlantic, West Africa has also seen a resurgence in activity. Mining operations, which had previously slowed their output amid the extreme volatility of bunker prices, have returned to the market with fresh inquiries. It has been a cautiously active week in the USG Handy market, the tonnage count is slightly down from last week, and while market circulated orders have also been lower than last week, there have been some orders that charterers have kept off market. A few charterers have found themselves needing spot/ppt replacements, and others have requirements for early May loading dates that they are keeping behind the curtains. Overall sentiment remains quietly positive, with owners continuing to push firmer ideas amid a relatively balanced position list. Fuel uncertainty continues to weigh on sentiment across the region as the market keeps a close eye on developments in the Middle East. We are seeing Trans-Atlantic trips rate for USD 13,000 – in line with levels at the start of the week. On the Supramax and Ultramax market, conditions have remained firm. While fresh 1– 10 May positions have entered the market, increased inter-Caribbean enquiry has helped support rates, pushing levels into the mid USD 20,000s. We are also seeing Trans-Atlantic trips fixing at around USD 30,000 on an Ultramax. Fronthaul activity, however, remains limited. A pronounced “tonnage shortage” sentiment emerged, particularly in Southeast Asia and the North Pacific. Previously suppressed trading demand was released in a concentrated manner, and when combined with temporary tightness in vessel supply, drove the market sharply higher within a short period, resulting in a clear upward shift in the earnings benchmark. The Indonesian coal sector was the first to reflect this upward momentum. As fresh cargoes gradually entered the market while early-positioned tonnage in Southeast Asia remained limited, the resulting supply-demand mismatch pushed rates higher. The Indo/SE Asia route strengthened continuously from the beginning of the week, with reported fixtures such as an SMX open Weda fixing in the high USD 18k range for Indo/Thai, and another SMX open Obi Island fixing up to USD 20k, highlighting strong regional demand and rapid tonnage absorption. On the Indo/China route, although domestic supply-demand fundamentals remained relatively balanced and import demand was not particularly strong, freight levels still increased notably in line with the broader market. The Indo/India route showed the most significant gains, with rates leading the rally and even surpassing the USD 30k mark. Reported fixtures include a UMX open Philippines fixing at USD 31k for Indo/Bdesh, as well as an SMX delivery Singapore on subs above USD 30k for Indo/WCI, clearly reflecting robust demand from the Indian subcontinent and a tight tonnage situation. The North Vietnam/South China region continued to act as a core supporting pillar for the market, maintaining high levels of activity. Clinker exports from Vietnam to Bangladesh remained strong, with rates moving further upward, including a reported UMX open Zhoushan fixing around USD 26k for clinker via South China to Bdesh. At the same time, nickel ore shipments sustained strong momentum, with SMX open South China fixing at USD 19k+ for nickel ore to China, continuing to absorb regional tonnage. In addition, backhaul demand to the United States also strengthened, with a UMX open Yangjiang fixing at USD 21k for steels to USEC, indicating solid support from long-haul demand. The NOPAC market remained stable overall. Although trading activity was relatively limited, freight levels moved upward in line with the broader market trend. UMX open Far East fixtures were reported at USD 19k+ for NOPAC round voyages, providing a solid floor for the market. North China steel and general cargo exports strengthened significantly this week, particularly on routes to the Red Sea and the Mediterranean. Fixtures included an SMX open North China fixing around USD 22k to the Mediterranean via Goa with bagged cargo, and another SMX open Zhoushan fixing around USD 19k to the Mediterranean via Goa with steels, demonstrating strong long-haul demand pulling tonnage away from the region. Bulk cargoes also remained firm, with a UMX open North China fixing around USD 27k for a trip to Bangladesh with slag, indicating a market that was not only strong but arguably approaching overheated levels. The Australian market also maintained a firm tone this week, with stable cargo flows from the supply side. Grain and salt from Western Australia, coal from Eastern Australia, and minerals from Northern Australia continued to move steadily, providing consistent support to the regional market and lifting overall freight levels. A reported fixture includes a UMX open Philippines fixing around USD 23.5k for WAus/China salt, reflecting the broader strength across routes. In the period market, strength persisted throughout the week. Supported by the rising spot market and firm FFA levels, period rates continued to climb. UMX short period fixtures were commonly concluded at USD 20k–21k, while one-year period rates increased to USD 18.5k+, reflecting strong owner confidence in the near- to mid-term outlook and a clear reluctance to commit tonnage. Overall, the Pacific Supramax market this week was characterized by rapid gains and broad-based strength, driven by concentrated demand release and temporary tightness in vessel supply. In the short term, with cargo volumes continuing to emerge and market sentiment remaining strong, the market is expected to stay elevated, with potential for further upside. However, caution is warranted regarding the risk of a short-term correction following the sharp rally, as well as the impact of macroeconomic developments on market dynamics. ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场整体承压但分化明显，好望角型和巴拿马型船指下跌，超灵便型和灵便型则逆势上扬。好望角型受大西洋地区需求疲软拖累，现货市场活跃度低；巴拿马型亚洲市场保持坚挺，印尼出口活跃支撑运价；超灵便型和灵便型市场情绪积极，美国海湾地区基本面强劲。FFA曲线全线下移，市场对短期前景趋于谨慎。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: BDI下跌8点至2665，好望角型领跌（-33），但超灵便型（+13）和灵便型（+6）表现韧性。吨位供需呈现区域分化：好望角型太平洋市场平稳但大西洋走软；巴拿马型亚洲强欧洲弱；灵便型美国海湾基本面坚实。FFA市场全面回调显示市场对Q2-Q3预期降温。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: 好望角型C5航线（西澳-青岛）维持在$13.00附近僵持，大西洋C3航线买卖双方报价差距扩大至$1.50。巴拿马型太平洋持续走强（P3A+$86，P5+$220），但期租市场（P5TC -$44）和FFA曲线同步走弱预示短期压力。超灵便型（S1_63/S2_63）逆势上扬反映亚洲煤炭/镍矿贸易支撑。灵便型大西洋持续强劲，美国海湾运费稳固。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注C3大西洋航线买卖价差收窄情况（当前$32.50对$34.00），以及5月装港船舶供应收紧能否提供支撑。巴拿马型关注亚洲市场持续性（P3A测试$18,000+），警惕北太平洋和印尼贸易流变化。FFA曲线Cape和Panamax中远期贴水结构加深，建议关注Q2-Q3合约价差交易机会。

market_watch: C3大西洋航线报价分歧扩大至$1.50，关注周五收盘能否收窄
巴拿马型P3A/P5本周强势但P5TC期租回调，注意短端波动风险
FFA曲线全面下移，Cape May26跌破31,500支撑位
超灵便型S2_63（北中国-澳洲往返）大涨$343，表现突出
印尼煤炭/铝土矿出口活跃，支撑东南亚航次需求

route_focus.view: 图巴朗-青岛航线指数跌至$33.07，买卖双方报价差距扩大至$1.50水平，显示市场参与者在价格上存在明显分歧，短期方向不明确，需等待新的催化剂。
跨大西洋往返航线报价14,416对15,000，买卖双方僵持，租家压价意愿明显但船东挺价，成交量偏低，短期可能维持区间震荡。
Skaw-Passero至里约热内卢航线本周零波动收于7,914，欧洲地中海区域活动平稳，暂无明显方向，等待更多货盘指引。
